The hub's own measurement overrides the public default only when each arm it compares ran at least 100 shared cases: fewer leave an interval wider than the gaps between the arms (30 cases give a 95 percent interval of about plus or minus 17 points).

Fit of evidence (added 2026-11-10 after the first ranking was seen, because that ranking would have raised cost for an install with one provider): a tier selects its default from public numbers only when evaluations marked direct (they measure the tier's own kind of call) carry at least this share of its capability weight; otherwise the held default stays and the proxy ranking is returned for information.

Effort must be real (added 2026-11-10 after the first ranking was seen): an arm at an effort other than the model's default is eligible only when the caller for its provider applies the effort the chooser returns; today no caller applies a per-call effort, so only each model's default effort competes, and the cost the metric assumed is the cost paid.
